short: The free group factors are isomorphic

title.title: The free group factors are all isomorphic
title.subtitle: Claim: $L(\mathbb F_n) \cong L(\mathbb F_{n+1})$ for $n \ge 3$, hence every $L(\mathbb F_r)$, $1 < r \le \infty$, is one factor

beats.text: Interpolated free group factors: either all the same, or all different (1994)
Claim: $L(\mathbb F_n) \cong L(\mathbb F_{n+1})$ for $n \ge 3$; amplifying by $\sqrt2$ reaches $\mathbb F_2$
So every $L(\mathbb F_r)$, $1 < r \le \infty$, is one and the same factor

achievement.label: Free group factor problem (credited to Kadison)
statement: L(\mathbb F_2) \cong L(\mathbb F_3) \cong \cdots \cong L(\mathbb F_\infty)
achievement.context: Before: all isomorphic or pairwise different (Dykema, Radulescu 1994); most expected different
achievement.note: Free entropy dimension is not an invariant of the generated algebra

plain: Algebras built from free groups with 2, 3 or more generators were thought to differ; claim: all the same

steps: Start with the extra generator and the n others, all free
Nudge the others slightly so a word in them mimics the extra one
Repeat with shrinking errors: n generators do the work of n+1

voice.text: Free group factors were known to be all equal or all different. Which one?
Nudge the generators so a word mimics one extra; repeat with shrinking errors.
Claimed: they are all the same factor.
